truncate

TRUN-kayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To truncate is to shorten by cutting off part of something.

The editor had to truncate the rambling speech down to a tight two minutes for broadcast.

Worked Example

The database truncated every customer's name to twenty characters, accidentally cutting off half the last names on the list.

Truncate describes shortening something, often a text, list, or process, by cutting off its end or top, rather than simply trimming a little from throughout.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

abbreviate: To abbreviate is to squeeze something into a compact written form -- Doctor becomes Dr., a long title becomes its initials -- so the whole meaning is kept, just written smaller. To truncate is blunter: the end is cut off and simply lost, the way a report loses its final pages.

shorten: To shorten is the general word for making anything shorter, by any method and from anywhere -- the middle, the edges, the end. To truncate is one specific way of shortening: cutting off the end or the top in a single lop, so the tail is gone entirely.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extend: make something longer

expand: make something larger or more complete

Where it sits · how much of it is removed — trim → truncate → eliminate

trim vs. truncate: Trim is gentler than truncate: trimming shaves a small, even amount from the edges, while truncating lops off a whole end of something in a single cut.

eliminate vs. truncate: To eliminate something removes it entirely, rather than simply cutting off part of it the way truncating does.

The pieces

root — trunc

root — trunc: maimed, cut short; a tree trunk (Latin (truncus))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to cause (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: trunc ("cut short") + -ate = to make something cut short.

Use the root in a new word: trunk

Use the root in a new word: trunk: The same root gives us "trunk," the main stem of a tree or the main part of the human body -- both are the central part left after the branches or limbs are set aside.
